statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. CME's daily maintenance halt covers the current hour, so no NQ price discovery is taking place. The reference point is the 28,945.06 cash close, up 0.02%, reached after a 192-point recovery off the 28,753.29 session low that invalidated the post-press-conference one-way leg. VIX closed at 17.71 against an 18.94 session high, and the 2-year settled at 4.736%, marginally below the 4.742% 52-week high it set intraday. Tail returns to the low band while Stress stays high, because the front-end repricing from the hike is still unretraced.
recommendation: Tail moves into the low band for the current hour on evidence that was verified after the cash close rather than on any assumption about the overnight. The index recovered 192 points off its low into the close, implied volatility decayed from an 18.94 high to 17.71, crude fell 3.60% on a reported partial restart of the damaged Saudi East-West pipeline, and the 2-year eased fractionally to 4.736% from the 4.742% high it printed intraday. The current hour additionally carries no price-path risk of its own because CME's daily maintenance halt suspends trading in the reference contract until 22:00 UTC. What remains unresolved is the front end, which is why Stress stays in the high band and the mapped state is described as a return to the low band rather than an all-clear. The narrow danger window covers the 22:00 UTC Globex reopen, the first post-FOMC price discovery after the halt. The highest modelled risk in the forward path is the 13:30 UTC cash open on September 17, which follows the first post-hike data block by one hour; that remains a conditional checkpoint and no opening continuation is treated as observed.
headline: Nasdaq-100 holds its flat 28,945.06 close through the CME maintenance halt as volatility decays and the 2-year slips fractionally off its 52-week high
body: The FOMC raised the federal funds target range by 25 basis points to 3.75-4.00% at 18:00 UTC in a unanimous 12-0 vote, the first hike in three years, stating that inflation remains elevated and that the action supports a timelier return to the 2 percent goal. The initial reaction was risk-positive and then reversed sharply during Chair Warsh's press conference, carrying the index from 29,235.89 to a 28,753.29 low. The decisive evidence for the current assessment is what followed: the Nasdaq-100 recovered 192 points into the 20:00 UTC cash close to finish at 28,945.06, up 0.02%, so the pathological no-retracement path scored two hours ago did not persist. The current hour adds a second, structural reason for a lower reading. CME's daily maintenance halt runs from 21:00 to 22:00 UTC, and both futures quote sources stop at a last print of 29,263.75, timestamped 20:59:59 UTC, against a futures session range of 29,053.00 to 29,549.75. There is therefore no live price path in this hour to score, and no exposure in the reference contract until the Globex reopen. Cross-asset evidence continued to improve into and after the close. VIX finished at 17.71 after trading as high as 18.94. WTI fell 3.60% to $102.02 and Brent 2.90% to $105.60 after reports that Saudi Aramco is working to bypass a damaged section of the 1,200-kilometre East-West pipeline and restore roughly half its capacity within days, with full restoration targeted in about six weeks. That removes part of the acute supply premium built up while the Strait of Hormuz has been closed, though the underlying conflict remains an open overnight headline channel. Rates are the one component that has not stabilised in the same way. The 2-year closed at 4.736%, up 7.3 basis points on the day and only fractionally below the 4.742% 52-week high it printed intraday, while the 10-year holds above 5.00%. Breadth also remains poor and unresolved: the Dow fell 1.21% to 51,461.90 and the S&P 500 0.45% to 7,551.81 against a Nasdaq Composite that closed down 0.01%, so the index-level recovery was concentrated in megacap technology and semiconductors, where delayed latest-session context shows Intel up 3.99% and AMD up 1.72%. The combination of an observed and completed retracement, decaying implied volatility, an easing oil premium and a halted reference contract supports a low-band Tail for this hour, while the unretraced front-end move and the narrow breadth keep Stress in the high band. No Nasdaq-100 megacap reports earnings tonight, so the overnight is catalyst-light until the 12:30 UTC release block on September 17.

lookbackSummary: Across the past 24 hours the published Claude state opened at 17 at Tuesday's post-close hour, eased through the low band overnight and bottomed at 13 at 01:00 UTC while the Asian and European sessions held a contained normal range, running 14-16 through the European morning. It returned to the watch band at 12:00 UTC with the U.S. pre-market, held 20-22 through the afternoon and rose to 24 at 18:00 UTC as the FOMC statement landed. The single highest reading of the window was 31 at 19:00 UTC, published while the index sat at its session low during the Warsh press conference with no retracement yet formed. That reading captured the structure observed at the time; the 192-point recovery into the cash close then invalidated its continuation premise, and the 20:00 UTC reading fell back to 20. The current hour steps down again to 18.
outlookSummary: The forecast opens at 18 for the current halt hour, rises to 21 for the 22:00 UTC Globex reopen, which is the narrow danger window and the first post-FOMC price discovery after the halt, then settles to a 17 overnight floor across the Asian session. That floor sits slightly above a typical quiet night because live Middle East supply headlines remain an open channel, not because of any observed index structure. The path drifts to 18-19 through the European morning, then rises to 22 for the 12:00 UTC hour containing jobless claims, the Philadelphia Fed index, housing starts and building permits, and peaks at 24 for the 13:30 UTC cash open, the highest modelled value in the window because a post-policy-shift opening auction is where one-way structure would establish if it is going to. That peak is explicitly conditional. The path then decays through 22, 21 and 20 across the U.S. morning, returns to 19 from 17:00 UTC, and lifts once more to 20 for the closing power hour on structural rebalancing grounds. Stress stays in the high band at both ends of the window, easing to a 64-65 elevated-band trough overnight before rebounding to 76 at the open, reflecting an environment that remains difficult without implying a lethal price path.
